sections.title: 🎯 What You'll Learn
sections.content:
Today, you'll discover how to write conditions in a single line—like a shortcut for decisions!

• What the ternary operator is and how it works
• How to replace simple if-else statements with it
• When to use (and not use) this compact syntax

sections.title: 💡 Concept Explanation
sections.content:
Imagine you're at a coffee shop. The barista asks: "Do you want sugar?" Instead of saying "If I want sugar, add it; else, skip it," you simply say "Yes or no?" The ternary operator works the same way—it’s a quick yes/no decision maker for your code.

Here’s the magic formula:
`condition ? valueIfTrue : valueIfFalse`

• **Condition**: A true/false check (like `age >= 18`)
• **?**: The "decision point" (like asking "Is this true?")
• **valueIfTrue**: What to do if the condition is true
• **valueIfFalse**: What to do if the condition is false

sections.title: 📊 Visual Simulation
sections.content: Step-by-step visualization of how Conditional Expressions works:

steps.title: Check the Condition
steps.description: The code evaluates if the condition is true or false. Think of it like a traffic light: green (true) or red (false).
steps.code:
int age = 20;
boolean isAdult = age >= 18; // true

steps.title: Pick the Right Path
steps.description: If the condition is true, the code picks the first value after `?`. If false, it picks the value after `:`.

steps.title: Result!
steps.description: The ternary operator returns the chosen value. Here, `message` becomes "Welcome!" because `isAdult` is true.

sections.title: ⚡ Key Points
points: ✓ It’s a shortcut for simple if-else statements
✓ Only use it for short, clear decisions—don’t nest them!
✓ Works with any type: numbers, strings, booleans, etc.

sections.title: 🔥 Tips & Mistakes
dos: Assign the result to a variable for clarity
donts: Don’t nest ternary operators (it gets messy!)
Avoid using it for complex logic
Don’t forget the `:`—it’s easy to miss!
sections.protip: If your ternary operator spans more than one line, it’s probably better as an if-else statement.

sections.title: 🌍 Real World Use
sections.content: Where is Conditional Expressions used in real apps?

examples.how: Show a "Login" button if the user isn’t logged in, or "Welcome back!" if they are.
Display "Free Shipping!" if the cart total is over $50, or "Add $X more for free shipping."
Set a player’s score multiplier to 2x if they have a power-up, or 1x if they don’t.

problem.description: Write a ternary operator to check if a number is even or odd. If it’s even, return "Even"; if odd, return "Odd".
hints: Remember the ternary syntax: `condition ? valueIfTrue : valueIfFalse`
problem.explanation: The condition `number % 2 == 0` checks if the number is even. If true, it returns "Even"; otherwise, "Odd".

sections.title: 📝 Summary
points: 📌 Practice with even/odd checks, user statuses, or discounts
📌 Next up: Combining conditions with logical operators!
